course.title: Git — Complete Deep Developer Tools Course
course.description: A Git-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with detailed concepts, practical workflows, dedicated tasks, troubleshooting, security and a production learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the tool properly; no fixed cross-tool template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Use the tool confidently in professional development.
Complete a production-style developer workflow capstone.

modules.title: Version Control Foundations
modules.description: Repositories, commits, working tree, staging area and why version control matters.

lessons.title: Version Control Foundations
lessons.description: Repositories, commits, working tree, staging area and why version control matters.
learningObjectives: Apply it to a realistic development workflow.

notes.text: Repositories, commits, working tree, staging area and why version control matters.
Learn version control foundations by understanding the developer problem first, then the tool concept, then a realistic command/editor workflow, and finally how it fits into professional development.

Version Control Foundations is a practical part of a modern development workflow. Students should understand not only the command or editor feature, but also why it is used, what it changes, how to verify it and how to recover from mistakes.

notes.caption: Add a clear diagram or screenshot-style teaching visual explaining Version Control Foundations.

items: Understand the underlying developer problem.
Know the important concepts and terminology.
Use the tool safely and intentionally.
Verify the result instead of assuming success.
Understand recovery and troubleshooting.

notes.code:
Scenario: Create a repository and explain its three main local states.

Workflow: inspect state -> perform action -> verify output -> test failure/recovery -> document.

items: Define the goal.
Inspect the current state.
Choose the smallest correct command/tool action.
Run it and inspect the result.
Test an edge case or failure.
Recover safely if something goes wrong.
Document the workflow.
Running commands without checking the current state.
Using destructive operations without understanding them.
Ignoring permissions and security.
Mixing environment-specific configuration into source code.
Skipping verification after changes.
Inspect before modifying.
Prefer reversible operations when possible.
Keep credentials and secrets out of repositories.
Use consistent team conventions.
Automate repeatable checks.
Document important workflows.
I can explain Version Control Foundations in my own words.
I can perform the basic workflow.
I can verify the result.
I can identify a risky/failure case.
I know how to recover or troubleshoot.
